title: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even chunks. Put them in a large pot of cold salted water, bring to the boil and cook for about 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.

While the potatoes cook, heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the pork sausages, turning often, for 10 to 12 minutes until browned all over and cooked through. Move them to a plate and cover loosely with foil.

Halve, peel and thinly slice the brown onions. Melt half the butter in the same pan over medium-low heat and cook the onions with a pinch of salt, stirring now and then, for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and golden. Crush in the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Sprinkle the plain flour over the onions and stir for 1 to 2 minutes to cook it out.

Pour in the beef stock a little at a time, whisking between additions so no lumps form. Stir in the worcestershire sauce and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the gravy thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Drain the potatoes and let them steam dry in the pot for a minute. Mash with the remaining butter and the milk until smooth, then season well with salt and pepper.
Return the sausages and any resting juices to the pan and turn them through the gravy for 2 minutes to warm through.
Pile the mash onto plates, sit the sausages on top and spoon over plenty of onion gravy.
